summary: Implemented the rich.progress open/wrap_file feature across rich/progress.py, tests/test_progress.py, docs/source/progress.rst, and CHANGELOG.md. Nothing was run (no tests, black, or mypy), and nothing was committed. Key choices: name/mode properties added on the reader because typing.IO declares them abstract; io.open used inside progress.py to avoid the shadowed builtin; mypy category names used for suppressions (override, no-untyped-def, attr-defined); no return suppression on module-level open since the context wrapper should match structurally. Some docstring lines exceed 88 columns, matching track()'s existing style. The tests and type checks still need to be run by the user.
